findings_qualitative.value: 195616 is an unobscured, quenching galaxy with low gas fraction; 209435 is a heavily obscured, actively star-forming, gas-rich UMG; both host AGN

evidence.quote: our analysis reveals that 195616 is an unobscured galaxy undergoing quenching, and 209435 is a heavily obscured, actively star-forming UMG.

claims.hypothesis: UV-NIR-only classification of the two UMGs as quiescent is correct
claims.experiment: Add ten FIR-to-radio bands and refit with CIGALE
claims.result: 209435 SFR rises from <=14 to 389 Msun/yr; 195616 SFR 62.5 Msun/yr
claims.finding: 209435 is a dusty star-forming UMG, 195616 is quenching

evidence.quote: we are able to definitively classify 209435 as a heavily dusty star-forming UMG and 195616 as a less-dusty quenching (rather than quenched) UMG.

claims.hypothesis: The two UMGs differ in gas content
claims.experiment: RJ-tail dust continuum gas masses compared to A3COSMOS
claims.finding: 195616 is gas-poor, 209435 gas-rich with t_dep 1.44 Gyr

evidence.quote: has a very low gas-to-stellar mass ratio ($M_{\rm mol}/M_{\star} = 0.12 \pm 0.03$)

claims.experiment: SED AGN fractions, X-ray, radio, emission lines
claims.result: MIR AGN fractions >70%; 195616 X-ray AGN; both radio-quiet
claims.finding: AGN in both; feedback may have depleted gas in 195616

evidence.quote: We presented multi-pronged evidence for significant AGN activity in both UMGs

why_this_data.value: Public FIR-to-radio data needed to distinguish quiescent from dust-obscured star-forming galaxies

evidence.quote: To conclusively distinguish quiescent galaxies from dust-obscured starbursts and to assess the role of AGN, it is essential to incorporate longer wavelength observations.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Charlot & Fall attenuation gives 0.5 dex higher stellar mass for 209435; deferred to future work

evidence.quote: the (cite: CharlotFall2000) attenuation model resulted in an estimate of stellar mass 0.5 dex higher

limitations_admitted.value: A3COSMOS gas masses do not include AGN contribution; AGN may bias gas mass of 195616

evidence.quote: the (cite: Liu2019b) approach does not include any possible AGN contribution, which may lead to overestimates of both SFR and molecular gas mass.

Results depend on attenuation law choice
